from.place: Proof opening: Choose a compactification c=(j,p); the local compact-support-extension and cofiltered-coherent-diagram splits require coherent comparisons of this choice. This is an agent-added foundation, not a WANTED quotation from the blueprint.

proof.text: Construct a simplicial set $E$ by taking $E_k$ to be the maps $u:\Delta^{k+1}\to Q$ with last vertex $t$. For a monotone map $\alpha:[l]\to[k]$, extend it by $\alpha^+(l+1)=k+1$ and put $E(\alpha)(u)=u\circ\Delta(\alpha^+)$. Since $(\alpha\beta)^+=\alpha^+\beta^+$, these operators satisfy the simplicial identities. Restriction to the initial face $\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,k\}}$ defines a simplicial map $q:E\to Q$: restricting $u\circ\Delta(\alpha^+)$ to that face gives $(q(u))\circ\Delta(\alpha)$. All constructions use the simplices and operators of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proof, construction of the vertex slice and its projection; explicit degreewise version.

proof.text: The map $q$ is a right fibration. Indeed, for a square against $\Lambda_i^k\hookrightarrow\Delta^k$ with $k\ge1$ and $0<i\le k$, the prescribed slice faces give the faces of $\Delta^{k+1}$ numbered $j\ne i,k+1$, and the bottom simplex gives face $k+1$. They agree on intersections by the simplicial identities and the square. Their union is precisely $\Lambda_i^{k+1}$; its last vertex is $t$. Since $0<i<k+1$, the quasicategory axiom in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] fills this inner horn, giving the required lift in $E$. To fill an inner horn in $E$, first fill its projection in $Q$ and then use this right-fibration lifting property. Hence $E$ is a quasicategory as well.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.1, vertex-slice special case, proved here directly by the horn-face calculation.

proof.text: For each vertex $x\in Q$, the degree-$k$ fiber $E_x=\{x\}\times_QE$ consists exactly of those $u:\Delta^{k+1}\to Q$ whose whole initial face is constant at $x$ and whose last vertex is $t$. Its operators are the $\alpha^+$ of Step 1, so it is literally the right-pinched space $\operatorname{Map}_Q(x,t)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Apply only the Kan-fiber clause of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers], taking its $B=Q$, $E=F$ equal to the constructed $E$, and both projections equal to $q$. Step 2 supplies the quasicategory and right-fibration hypotheses. Thus every $E_x$ is Kan, without a nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Construction 4.6.5.1; Kan fibers as in Proposition 4.6.5.5 (01L0), supplied by the cited fiber theorem.

proof.text: For $k\ge0$, a lifting square $\partial\Delta^k\to E$ over $b:\Delta^k\to Q$ is exactly a map $\partial\Delta^{k+1}\to Q$ with last vertex $t$: its coned faces numbered $0,\ldots,k$ come from the top boundary map, and its initial face numbered $k+1$ is $b$. The former agree on their intersections by simpliciality of the top map, and agree with $b$ on their initial faces by commutativity of the square. Conversely restrict such a boundary to those coned faces to recover the top map and to the initial face to recover $b$. A lift is in either description a single $(k+1)$-simplex extending all these faces. For $k=0$ the data are just the two vertices $b(0),t$, and a lift is an edge $b(0)\to t$. Consequently the boundary-extension condition of the item is equivalent to $q$ being a trivial Kan fibration in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], including its dimension-zero surjectivity clause.

source.place: Proof, equivalence of the displayed boundary and relative lifting conditions, specialized to n=-2; all faces and k=0 written explicitly.

proof.text: Assume every $\operatorname{Map}_Q(x,t)$ is contractible. By Step 3 these are exactly the Kan vertex fibers of the right fibration $q$. Here contractible means weakly contractible by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] therefore hold, and its conclusion says $q$ is a trivial Kan fibration. The explicit correspondence of Step 4 supplies every required extension in $Q$.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.14, implication (3) to (1), applied to the vertex slice used in 05ET.

proof.text: Conversely assume the boundary-extension condition. Step 4 gives all boundary lifts for $q$. Fix $x\in Q_0$. Given $a:\partial\Delta^k\to E_x$, compose it into $E$ and take the bottom simplex in $Q$ to be constant at $x$. A lift for $q$ then lands in $E_x$, so $E_x\to\Delta^0$ lifts every boundary, including $k=0$. It is a Kan fibration because $E_x$ is Kan by Step 3. Apply [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] to this map: its trivial-Kan-fibration clause implies it is a weak homotopy equivalence. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] this means $E_x$ is weakly contractible. Step 3 identifies $E_x$ with $\operatorname{Map}_Q(x,t)$, proving the assertion for every $x$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.7.6, trivial Kan implies weak homotopy equivalence, for each vertex fiber over a point.

proof_origin.place: Explicit n=-2 slice/boundary proof underlying Proposition 4.7.3.11 (06R1), using the existing right-fibration fiber criterion (01NU) for the forward direction and the Kan criterion (00ZP) for the reverse. Sources read online; archival copies WANTED in report.md.

title: Boundary extension criterion for a final vertex
statement: Use quasicategories and right-pinched mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $Q$ be a quasicategory and $t\in Q_0$. The spaces $\operatorname{Map}_Q(x,t)$ are contractible for every vertex $x$ if and only if, for every $m\geq1$ and simplicial map $\sigma:\partial\Delta^m\to Q$ whose last vertex is $t$, there exists an extension $\overline\sigma:\Delta^m\to Q$. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ denotes the union of the faces of $\Delta^n$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 4.7.3.11 (06R1), using Definition 4.7.3.1 of finality and the right-pinch comparison of Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5). This concerns a specified final vertex, not contractibility of the whole final-object subcategory.
